title: At least 30 people killed after high-speed trains collide in central Spain
summary: At least 30 people have been killed in a train crash in central Spain, local authorities have confirmed. Rail services between Madrid and Seville have been suspended.

image.caption: Ten people have been killed in a train crash in Spain which has seen several such accidents in recent yearsImage: Juanma Jiménez/EUROPA PRESS/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: We have moved our coverage to a live updates. Please join us here.
At least 30 people were killed in a train crash in central Spain on Wednesday morning, local authorities have confirmed.

"The information we are receiving is not good at all," a spokeswoman for the government of the Castilla-La Mancha region told local media, giving an initial death toll of ten which has since increased to "at least 30."

"There has been a collision between two trains [and] there are injured people," added Manuel Galans, mayor of the town of Urda in the province of Toledo, near to where the incident took place just after 9 a.m. local time.
The mayor of another nearby village, Jesus Perez of Los Yebenes, told Spanish TV that the accident appeared "serious."
Spanish Health Minister Monica Garcia told local broadcaster TVE that it was a "high impact accident, it will be a major tragedy" but said it was too soon to confirm a final casualty figure.
"We don't just need help from nearby hospitals, we need nearby hospitals that have ICU beds," she added.
Spain train crash: what do we know?
The cause of the collision was not immediately known, but initial reports suggested one train had slammed into the back of another train which had been stationary.

"We heard a massive roar, a truly ​enormous thud ‌that went on for 10 seconds as if the train were about to derail," one passenger, Miguel, told local radio station COPE. "Through the right-hand window, we could see a wrecked train – I imagine it must have been the other one."
Images from the scene showed at least two severely damaged train carriages flipped over on their side after tumbling down an embankment.

One of the trains, operated by AVE, was reportedly carrying 397 passengers while the other, operated by IRYO, had 146 people on board, according to the Castilla-La Mancha local government spokeswoman.
A reporter for local broadcaster TVE described scenes of "absolute chaos" and a constant stream of ambulances and emergency vehicles.
El Pais cited witnesses describing numerous injuries and ​arrival of emergency medical teams at the scene.

"All resources are currently being deployed," spokesperson for the Spanish emergency services told the AFP news agency, including "several fire crews, three helicopters, and two mobile intensive care units."
In a post on social media, rail operator Adif confirmed that "traffic ​on the Madrid-Andalusia high-speed rail line ​has been suspended following a rear-end collision ​between two trains."
Spanish PM Sanchez 'shocked' by 'serious' accident
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said he was "shocked" by the "serious" accident.

"Emergency services are working on the ground to assist those affected and ensure their safety, in coordination with all the involved administrations," he wrote on social media. "My affection, solidarity and support to all the victims and their families."
The collision comes just months after another devastating rail disaster near Adamuz in Andalusia in January.
In that accident, a high-speed train derailed and collided with an oncoming train, killing 46 people and injuring more than 150.
The crash was the deadliest in Spain since a 2013 crash that killed 80 people. The January incident shook the confidence the European country has in its extensive high-speed rail network.
